title: The Quiet Orbit Revisited
premise: Oscar Quintana, a clone of a murdered shipping magnate, has spent three years hiding in the margins of contested space, hauling cargo under a forged registry. When a manifest lists her original's killer—aboard a ship that was scrapped before it ever flew—she realizes someone is using her past as bait to draw her out. Pursued by both the fleet faction that murdered Quintana and the investigators who cloned her as evidence, she races toward a derelict relay at the edge of dead space where the truth of the murder is stored in an untransmitted black box. At the relay she discovers the killer is another clone of herself, grown by the murderers to replace the original and tie off loose ends; Oscar must choose between destroying the evidence that proves her own legal personhood and broadcasting it, which will end the fragile truce and ignite war. She broadcasts it anyway, accepting exile but gaining a found family among her ragtag crew who choose to follow her into the dark.
about_author: Dominic Okafor is a former maritime logistics analyst from Lagos who turned to science fiction after a decade spent tracking cargo through real-world contested waters. His novels are known for their blue-collar futurism, morally tangled protagonists, and quiet devotion to the families people build when institutions fail them.

chapters.title: Dead Registry
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar. Hauling scrap through the Meridian corridor, Oscar runs a routine customs scan and finds a name on her own manifest: Vess Andrade, the man convicted of murdering her original—listed aboard the Halcyon Drift, a ship decommissioned six years ago. The beat is cold dread beneath practiced calm; her invisibility has cracked.

chapters.title: Three Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar. Flashback-tinged chapter establishing her crew: engineer Sefa, pilot Brannoc, and medic Ilo, the found family who never ask about her face's famous original. Oscar almost tells them about the manifest and doesn't. Emotional beat: the ache of protecting people by lying to them.

chapters.title: The Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: POV: Sefa. Sefa digs into the Halcyon Drift's records and finds its transponder pinged last week—from inside dead space, where nothing flies. Someone is spoofing a ghost ship. Beat: loyalty tested; Sefa confronts Oscar gently, forcing her to admit the name on the manifest.

chapters.title: Warrant in the Wake
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar. A fleet patrol vessel hails them, citing an evidence-recovery warrant issued in Quintana's name—a case legally closed three years ago. The inspector, Adeyemi, boards and recognizes her face instantly. Beat: claustrophobic tension; Oscar realizes the fleet wants her, not the wreck.

chapters.title: Property of the Estate
chapters.summary: POV: Adeyemi. Adeyemi's POV reveals the fleet's internal fracture: one faction wants Oscar destroyed as a legal anomaly, another wants her testimony to reopen the murder case before the truce expires. He lets her go with a warning. Beat: uneasy alliance offered and distrusted.

chapters.title: Course to Dead Space
chapters.summary: POV: Brannoc. Brannoc plots the only route to the relay's last known coordinates through a debris field the truce forbids entering. The crew votes—unanimously—to go anyway. Beat: warmth and fear braided together; family means choosing danger together.

chapters.title: What the Clone Remembers
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar. In the long transit, Oscar confronts fragmentary inherited memories of Quintana's final day—Andrade's voice, a locked cabin, a second heartbeat in the room. Beat: identity horror; she cannot tell which memories are hers and which were installed.

chapters.title: The Salvage Claim
chapters.summary: POV: Ilo. Docking at a scavver station for fuel, Ilo trades medical work for intel and learns a bounty on 'the Quintana asset' has tripled overnight. A scavver crew tries to take them. Beat: violence erupting into the quiet life; Ilo kills for the first time to protect the crew.

chapters.title: Truce Clock
chapters.summary: POV: Adeyemi. Fleet chapters show the truce expiring in eleven days; hardliners plan to use the reopened Quintana case as casus belli regardless of what the relay holds. Adeyemi goes rogue, transmitting Oscar the relay's true coordinates. Beat: an enemy becoming something like an ally.

chapters.title: Ghost Signal
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar. They intercept the Halcyon Drift's phantom signal—and it answers, speaking in Quintana's voice, reciting coordinates only the original knew. Beat: vertigo; the dead are talking, and Oscar is being summoned home to a murder scene.

chapters.title: The Debris Field
chapters.summary: POV: Brannoc. A brutal navigation sequence through the graveyard of the last war; the ship takes damage, Sefa is injured shielding the drive core. Beat: sacrifice made concrete; the cost of the journey written in blood and hull plating.

chapters.title: Interrogation of One
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar. While Sefa heals, Oscar interrogates herself aloud with Ilo: if the memories are planted, is she a witness or a weapon? If they're real, is she Quintana or his daughter or no one? Beat: the theme of identity laid bare without resolution.

chapters.title: Adeyemi's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV: Adeyemi. Adeyemi rendezvouses mid-route, offering fleet protection in exchange for exclusive access to the black box. Oscar refuses custody of her own truth. Beat: power struggle between allies; trust extended on credit.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar. They reach the derelict relay—intact, powered, and waiting. Docking clamps engage without being hailed. Inside, lights come on in sequences Quintana would recognize. Beat: dread transformed into terrible welcome; the trap was always open.

chapters.title: Andrade
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar. In the relay's core they find Vess Andrade—or a body grown around his conviction, another engineered copy, kept alive as a living confession. He doesn't remember killing anyone. Beat: pity for the monster; the crime itself may have been performed by clones on both sides.

chapters.title: The Black Box
chapters.summary: POV: Sefa. Sefa cracks the relay archive: recordings prove Quintana's murder was ordered by the fleet faction now pushing for war, and the clone program was built to erase every witness—including Oscar. Beat: revelation as detonation; the truth is worse than the mystery.

chapters.title: Two of Her
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar. A second Quintana clone—the 'successful' replacement, raised by the conspirators—arrives with a fleet strike team, sent to erase the relay and Oscar. Face to face with herself, Oscar sees the person she'd have become if survival had been outsourced. Beat: mirror horror; identity versus design.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar. Climax. With the strike team breaching, Oscar must choose: destroy the archive and keep the truce, or transmit everything and start a war that might also free every engineered person like her. She transmits. The other clone hesitates—and lets her. Beat: the price of survival paid in full view.

chapters.title: Expiry
chapters.summary: POV: Adeyemi. The broadcast hits every fleet channel as the truce formally expires. Hardliners move to fire; Adeyemi and sympathetic crews refuse the order, fracturing the fleet instead of the peace. Beat: chaos with a spine of hope; truth as a weapon that cuts both ways.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Name
chapters.summary: POV: Ilo. Escaping the burning relay, the crew tends wounds and buries Andrade's body in the debris field. Ilo reflects on how a clone, a deserter, and a scavver became kin. Beat: grief and gratitude; mourning even the enemy who was also made, not born.

chapters.title: The Long Way Around
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar. Offered amnesty and a hearing that could grant her legal personhood, Oscar declines the fleet's terms and chooses the open route instead—but sends her testimony ahead, unsigned, so others like her can claim their own names. Beat: freedom chosen over legitimacy; identity self-authored.

chapters.title: Quiet Orbit, New Heading
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar. Epilogue. The crew takes a small contract hauling seed stock to a frontier colony, unremarkable and unwatched—for now. Oscar signs the manifest with her own hand, her own name, no forgery. Final beat: the quiet she wanted, finally earned rather than hidden in.
